html:
A road and rail link across the Øresund strait between Copenhagen in Denmark and Malmö in Sweden, opened on 1 July 2000. It carries a motorway on its upper deck and a railway below.

The link is in three parts: a cable stayed bridge of almost 8 km from the Swedish side, an artificial island called Peberholm, and a tunnel of about 4 km into Denmark, so that the bridge does not block ships or the flight path of Copenhagen airport.

Skåne, the region around Malmö, was Danish until the Treaty of Roskilde gave it to Sweden in 1658. The bridge rejoined the two shores in daily life. Tens of thousands of people now cross it to work, and the two cities act as one region. It also became famous through the crime series The Bridge.
